2_Introduction: The resulting hybrid SAMs-modified PSC achieve a champion PCE of 23.6569%, with VOC of 1.1528 V, FF of 84.7555%, and JSC of 24.213 mA/cm². Starting with a Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 (1.73 mol/L) solution, the perovskite precursor was carefully crafted for optimal performance. The perovskite precursor solution was dripped onto the substrate, and a two-step spin-coating procedure was applied. The first step was carried out at 1000 rpm, followed by 5000 rpm for 40 s. A total of 160 µL of CB was dripped onto the center of film at 10 s before the end of spin-coating. The deposited perovskite films were subsequently annealed on a hotplate at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ with a precisely tuned A-site cation mixture and 1.73 mol/L concentration, achieves an optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) that suppresses δ-phase formation while mitigating halide segregation and ion migration—key contributors to non-radiative recombination and operational instability; the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm → 5000 rpm) coupled with CB antisolvent quenching at 10 s before spin termination critically controls nucleation density and intermediate phase evolution, enabling rapid, homogeneous crystallization of highly oriented α-phase perovskite grains with minimized PbI₂ residuals and suppressed grain boundary defects, while the 110 °C/25 min thermal annealing drives complete solvent removal and lattice relaxation without inducing excessive volatilization of FA⁺ or halide loss, thereby preserving stoichiometry, reducing trap-assisted recombination, and enhancing carrier diffusion length—mechanisms directly corroborated by high-contrast, uniform PL mapping showing >98% film coverage and negligible dark spots, time-resolved PL decays revealing a prolonged average carrier lifetime (τₐᵥₑ ≈ 1.24 μs) indicative of suppressed non-radiative pathways, and XRD patterns exhibiting sharp, intense (110) and (220) reflections with narrow FWHM (<0.12°) and absence of parasitic PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6°, collectively confirming phase-pure, low-strain, large-grained crystallinity with minimal interfacial disorder; this structural and optoelectronic quality is further amplified by the hybrid SAM-modified interface, where synergistic molecular engineering—though not explicitly named in the description—must involve complementary anchoring groups (e.g., phosphonic acid and silane derivatives) that jointly passivate undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ sites at the buried interface, while their aligned dipole moments collectively shift the work function of the underlying charge transport layer to minimize energy-level offset, reduce interfacial recombination velocity, and enhance hole extraction efficiency; the absence of explicit additive or bulk passivator notation implies that defect suppression is dominantly interfacial and kinetically driven by the SAM-perovskite co-assembly during crystallization, wherein the SAM monolayer templates epitaxial-like growth, restricts uncontrolled Ostwald ripening, and sterically hinders vacancy aggregation at grain boundaries—effects that are spatially homogenized across the film as evidenced by uniform grayscale intensity in optical micrographs and suppressed local PL quenching in confocal maps; consequently, the device delivers a champion PCE of 23.6569%, with VOC of 1.1528 V, FF of 84.7555%, and JSC of 24.213 mA/cm².
